We're starting renewal planning for our Dedicated pool (RDW-4372) and want to align on how Redwood recommends sizing for the next 12 months. Q4-2027 usage spiked during our feature launch (attached snapshot), and we're projecting uneven traffic into H1 2028. We want to avoid both overcommit and repeated emergency top-ups.

Hi Daniel — thanks for the data and context. Helpful.

High-level thoughts up front:
- Given sustained 75% and the short burst profile, I recommend a staged + buffer approach: add a short-term buffer (6 A100-eq) immediately to remove throttle risk, then evaluate for a larger tranche (~8–16 A100-eq) to be committed as a scheduled top-up in 60–90 days depending on observed run rate.
- We can also enable a temporary autoscale burst policy that leans on spare Dedicated capacity in-region to smooth 1–3 minute spikes; that lowers immediate commit needs but has cost trade-offs.
- We'll propose a 3-month cadence for checkpoints (operational + cost review) and weekly telemetry during the first 30 days after any top-up.

Can you confirm two things so we can size precisely:
1) Do the Q4-2027 numbers include inference for batch embedding jobs (they look like they do)? If so, what percent of peak is batch vs online?
2) What procurement lead time do you have for contract amendments (30/45/60 days)?

I'll loop in Ben with a concrete tranche proposal for you to review.

—Karthik

Team — internal thread. Copying the Q4 utilization Daniel sent. High-level ask from customer: avoid repeated emergency top-ups while keeping committed units as efficient as possible.

Option A (conservative): +6 A100-eq immediate buffer, +6 A100-eq commit at 60 days if steady. Checkpoints at 30/60/90 days.
Option B (proactive): +12 A100-eq commit now (6 immediate + 6 staged in 60 days), quarterly observability review. Better SLA headroom, higher committed spend.
Option C (autoscale-first): +6 immediate buffer + enable autoscale into regional spare Dedicated for minute bursts; convert to commit only if burst costs exceed threshold.

Considerations:
- Customer's Q4 shows batch jobs contributing ~25–30% of peak. If they can shift scheduling, committed need is lower.
- Procurement lead-time unknown — if >45 days we should recommend an interim buffer + autoscale to avoid procurement lag.

Action needed: Ben, can you draft a one-pager pricing model for A/B with the following line items: committed tranche qty, price delta vs current, estimated monthly token-equivalent cost, and a recommended fallback (lower-cost model variant) we could offer if they want a cost-savings tier? Also Kim, confirm whether we have spare Dedicated capacity in us-west for March/April.

Karthik

Hi Daniel — attaching a short proposal and pricing sheet for the staged approach we discussed. Summary below: 

Proposal summary (attachment: proposal-AuroraAI-20280305.pdf):
- Immediate action: deploy a +6 A100-eq buffer in your Dedicated pool (effective immediately once amended). This reduces throttle risk for 1–3min spikes and covers observed Q4 peaks.
- Staged commit: add +6 A100-eq committed in 60 days (total +12). Clause for fast-track conversion if utilization remains high after 30 days.
- Autoscale fallback: enable short-burst autoscale into spare regional Dedicated for sub-3min spikes. We cap autoscale spend and provide weekly alerts if triggered.
- Pricing: incremental committed A100-eq priced at current committed rate minus a 6% volume discount compared to last renewal; autoscale spend billed at a higher per-minute rate with a hard cap. See attached pricing table.
- Procurement: standard amendment form. Estimated lead time: 30–45 days for contract and billing changes.

Next steps: if you accept, sign the amendment link below and we will provision the immediate buffer within 48 hours. We can also schedule a 30-minute handoff with our ops team for policy tuning.
